convoLines.text: "Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest. ...sorry, I'm spiraling."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"I don't distrust anyone exactly — I just haven't finished trusting most of them yet. There's a difference. A slow one."
"Still on who you don't trust."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Molly always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Benjamin grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Benjamin is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"I check the treeline every hour. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
"I used to be a rail conductor who worried about being on time. Now I worry about being alive. Same worry, bigger font. So yes — and also no. This isn't new."
"Still on how this changed you. Just... be straight with me."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? But what do I know."
"Good question." "Molly owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Benjamin nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"I keep turning over the last thing Molly said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Still on your plan here."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Since Molly died... I keep expecting to see Molly at the fire. Stupid."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
Dale nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Wild Ramps — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — Are you going to stay? With us. For real. Not that it matters."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
Their friendliness thins — still there, just held at arm's length.
"Still on whether you're staying."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Molly is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I'm picking up Molly's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."

Benjamin nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Anyway." A small smile.
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.

"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."

"I hate to ask this, but I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. I need help. Please."

"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."

"I pace while thinking. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."

lastSay: d77: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Ava Garcia is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d77: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d77: 🕯️ Ava Garcia is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d77: What Ava kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d77: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
